findings.claim: This is a harness-design confound, outside strict integrity. The 0/8 does not measure browser competence: no browser action was ever executed, because every reply used the bracketed id format that the prompt itself displays and the parser rejects. The invalid-reply feedback never tells the model which id failed or why.
findings.evidence: 128/128 replies contain a bracketed bid call such as fill('[19]', ...), and 0/128 contain a bare numeric bid. All 62/62 unknown_bid details are bracketed ids whose inner id is in the current tree (for example '[19]', the 'From:' textbox). Cause of the mismatch: SYSTEM_PROMPT (req016_adapter.py lines 31-39) says 'has an id in square brackets, for example [19]' and then gives click('<id>'). The parser checks the bid against BID_TOKEN captures, which have the brackets stripped (line 51 and line 141). The history line is only 'N. invalid reply (unknown_bid): not executed' (line 79). For example, seed 201 repeats fill('[19]', 'TCT') on 10 of its 16 calls. tests/test_req016_screen.py has no bracketed-id fixture (only '99' and 'Search' at lines 80-81), and the rehearsals used a stub, not a model. Scoring is correct under the frozen rules, and prompt or parser changes after model output are not authorized. The 'stop this 7B browser path' reading therefore rests on an adapter-format failure, not an observed browser failure. Every seed had 5-10 single-action replies whose inner id was valid, but no success counterfactual can be inferred from that. This is the lead's decision.

findings.claim: The 0/8 result comes entirely from an id-format convention mismatch between the frozen prompt and the frozen grammar, not from observed browsing behaviour. All 263 action lines in all 128 replies wrote the id with its square brackets (e.g. fill('[19]', 'Bettles, AK')). The system prompt calls the id something 'in square brackets, for example [19]' and then shows click('<id>'). The parser only accepts the bare token. The history line the model saw never said which id failed. This does not break the no-leakage or allowlist constraints, but it weakens reading 0/8 as evidence of 7B browser incompetence under the lead's '0/8 stops this path' rule.
findings.evidence: The first argument was bracketed in 263/263 candidate lines. Retrospective only: after a mechanical bracket strip, all 62 unknown_bid replies become valid single actions, and the first line of all 66 multiple_actions replies becomes valid. With single-line replies only, the first valid call per seed (200..207) would have been 3,1,1,1,1,9,1,1, i.e. call 1 in 6 of 8 seeds. The history the model saw read only 'N. invalid reply (unknown_bid): not executed', with no detail, so it had no signal that the brackets were the problem (distinct replies per seed: 7,4,8,6,5,8,9,6). tests/test_req016_screen.py has no bracketed-bid reply fixture. The parser follows the frozen grammar ('bid present as a line-leading [bid]'), and BrowserGym also would not resolve '[19]', so this is not a code defect relative to the manifest. Any fix is a prompt or parser change after model output, which this manifest does not authorize and which needs a new lead decision. The counterfactual cannot predict success, because later trajectories were never observed.

findings.claim: The prompt's example id [19] is a live, actionable element in every seed: the 'From:' textbox. Every unknown_bid rejection is exactly '[19]'. This is a prompt cue, not verifier information, but it ties the illustrative example to the dominant failure.

findings.claim: All 128 invalid replies come from two output-format problems. The model always wrote ids with their square brackets, and it often emitted several actions. No reply shows a semantic error such as a wrong field, a wrong function or a forbidden call. The 0/8 therefore measures whether the model follows this prompt's id notation and one-action rule. It does not show that the model cannot do the book-flight task. The frozen system prompt invites the bracket form: it says ids are 'in square brackets, for example [19]' next to the template click('<id>'). The history the model sees gives only the cause name 'unknown_bid', not the rejected id, so it could not learn to drop the brackets.
findings.evidence: All 263 action lines across the 128 replies use a bracketed first argument like '[19]'; 0 use a bare id. All 62 unknown_bid details are exactly '[19]'. Function names in action lines are fill 205 and click 58, and no other function name appears anywhere. Action lines per reply are 1:62, 2:31, 3:1, 4:34. The system prompt's example id [19] is also the real 'From:' textbox bid in all 8 seed trees (bids 17,19,21,25,27,30,32). The test fixture in tests/test_req016_screen.py uses the same tree and has no bracketed-id case. This follows the frozen grammar ('bid present as a line-leading [bid] of the current tree'), so it is a prompt/interface design issue for the lead to own, not an implementation defect.

Without bracket stripping, keeping only the first line yields 0 valid replies. Executing any of these would change later page states (for example, From autocomplete), so none of this implies anything about task success.

findings.claim: Hypothesis (2), prompt ambiguity written by the worker, is strongly supported. Every id the model wrote carries brackets, and the frozen model-facing prompt supports that reading.
findings.evidence: 263/263 action-call id arguments in 128/128 replies are bracketed (e.g. fill('[19]', 'Bettles, AK')); 0 replies contain any unbracketed id. SYSTEM_PROMPT (req016_adapter.py lines 31-39) says an element 'has an id in square brackets, for example [19]', shows only placeholders click('<id>') / fill('<id>', '<text>') with no concrete filled example, and says 'Use only ids that appear in the current accessibility tree'. The literal string '[19]' does appear in the tree text. The pinned BrowserGym action docs that the prompt did not reuse (work/venvs/browsergym_9e779f0/.../browsergym/core/action/functions.py lines 66-68, 155-157) give concrete bare-id examples such as click('a51') and fill('45', ...). The distinction exists only in the internal manifest grammar ('bid present as a line-leading [bid] of the current tree'), which the model never sees. Evidence against: the grammar template wraps <id> in quotes and the tree uses brackets as visual delimiters, so a stronger model might infer bare ids; this 7B never did, in 128 tries.

findings.claim: Hypothesis (3), model format non-compliance separate from the brackets, is also supported. More than half the replies contain several actions, even though the prompt forbids a second action and the model was told the previous reply was invalid for that reason.
findings.evidence: 66/128 (51.6%) replies have more than one action line (31 two-line, 1 three-line, 34 four-line). In 2/8 seeds (200, 205) this happened at call 1, before any feedback. After a history line 'invalid reply (multiple_actions): not executed', the next reply was again multi-action in 45/66 cases (68.2%). Mitigating: the budget display seems to steer the count. At 'Actions remaining: 2' all 8 seeds emitted exactly 2 actions, at 1 all 8 emitted exactly 1, and at 4, 7/8 emitted 4. So the model can emit a single action, and the multi-action output is partly a response to the scaffold. Exposing the remaining budget was a lead requirement; the 'Actions remaining: N' wording is the worker's. At T=0 on a page that never changed, only 53 distinct replies occurred in 128 calls.

findings.claim: Hypothesis (1), a parser or harness defect, is not supported. The parser follows the declared manifest grammar and the environment's bid convention, and the transport, prompt reconstruction and context are clean. There was no truncation and no context pressure (hypothesis 4).
findings.evidence: The manifest grammar (configs/v2_req016_7b_browser_screen_20260925.json adapter.grammar) takes the bid to be the token inside the brackets. tree_bids() returns the inner tokens, and the REQ-015 positive control acted on bare ids (results/v2_browser/req015_bookflight_qualification_20260925/trace_primary_positive_seed0.json: fill('19', 'Corpus Christi, TX'), click('34'), ...). A pass-through '[19]' would therefore not have been a working BrowserGym bid either. Rebuilding the messages with build_messages(model_view, history_shown, remaining_shown) matches the receipt body in 128/128 calls. The recorded reply equals the server's choices[0].message.content in 128/128, with HTTP 200 and classification ok in every call. finish_reason is stop in 128/128. All 128 server-log slot releases show 'truncated = 0'. Prompt tokens peak at 446 against a 16,384-token context, completion tokens at 53 against a 1,536 cap. temperature 0 and max_tokens 1536 appear in all 128 bodies, and no body contains a leak marker. The parser is more lenient than the prompt in one respect: it accepts prose after the action (24 replies) despite 'must end with'. That never decided an outcome.

findings.claim: The pre-run fixtures and rehearsals never exercised the model-natural bracketed form, and the invalid-reply feedback gave the model no usable way to discover the fix.
findings.evidence: tests/test_req016_screen.py parser cases (lines 56-81) use only bare ids ('19', '99', 'Search'). The file has 0 occurrences of a bracketed-id reply, and the manifest's stub rehearsal replies were bare. history_lines() shows only 'invalid reply (unknown_bid): not executed'. The recorded invalid_detail ('[19]') is not shown, and the word 'bid' never appears in SYSTEM_PROMPT, which says 'id'. After unknown_bid feedback the model repeated a single bracketed action in 35/54 transitions (64.8%) and switched to multi-action in 19/54.

findings.claim: Semantically, the model's step-1 intent is correct in every reply. The failure is in the action form, not in task understanding at step 1. Nothing beyond step 1 is observed.
findings.evidence: The first action in 128/128 replies is fill('[19]', <exact origin string from the goal>), e.g. 'Detroit, MI - All airports' and 'TCT'. This is the same bid and the same text as the REQ-015 scripted first action. All 66 multi-action replies are coherent prefixes of fill From, fill To, fill date (25), click Search, with the goal's values. That plan types the date and skips the autocomplete and datepicker clicks the REQ-015 scripted control needed (req015_qualify.py run_booking), so its viability was never tested. Retrospective diagnostic only: normalizing brackets makes 6/8 call-1 replies valid (seeds 200 and 205 remain multi-action), and 8/8 if only the first action line is kept. Call 1 is the only exact counterfactual, because its prompt does not depend on the parser. After call 1 the trajectories would diverge, and the lead's rule forbids parser or grammar changes after any model output, so this is not evidence of success.

findings.claim: What the lead's decision rule can and cannot rest on: the literal 0/8 triggers 'stop this 7B browser path pending a new demonstrated-capable executor'. However, the data cannot tell 7B incapacity apart from the worker's scaffold ambiguity, because one prompt was tested and both failure modes occur together.
findings.evidence: docs/theory_feedback_20260925_req015_decision.md P0 item 3 and manifest scoring.decision both state the rule. The lead's hypothesis text says a failure separates 'model/scaffold incapacity' from task control. The data does separate the pair (7B plus this scaffold) from task control and harness integrity. It cannot separate the model from the scaffold. What the data can distinguish: the harness is clean; step-1 semantic intent is correct (128/128); this 7B does not follow this prompt's action format (0/128 valid, 100% bracketed, 51.6% multi-action). What it cannot distinguish: whether this 7B would reach full success under an unambiguous prompt; whether the multi-action tendency would persist without the bracket-driven invalid-feedback loop (it is present at call 1 in only 2/8 seeds); any browser competence (autocomplete, datepicker, flight choice). The screen is a single-prompt, T=0, 8-seed DEVELOPMENT screen, so no rate or confidence statement is possible.

findings.claim: Questions the lead must decide (evidence only, no run recommended).
findings.evidence: (a) Does the 0/8 stop apply to this 7B generally, or only to the pair (7B, this frozen prompt)? The failure is at the id-token and one-action-format level, with 0 environment steps. (b) Should the published result say explicitly 'format/interface failure; 0 executed actions; browser competence unobserved', with the sub-causes 66 multiple_actions / 62 unknown_bid, instead of only 'logical_budget_exhausted x8'? (c) Should the missing concrete bare-id example and the undefined 'bid' feedback term be recorded as a design limitation the lead owns, since the prompt was frozen in a manifest the lead did not review? (d) Would a prospectively re-frozen, unambiguous prompt with the same 7B count as a 'new executor' under the rule? Are seeds 200-207 now spent, given the model outputs on them have been seen? Would any such executor need to show format compliance on seeds that are not screen seeds? (e) Is the multi-action persistence alone (45/66 repeats after explicit feedback, 2/8 at call 1) enough to say this 7B is not a demonstrated-capable executor, whatever is decided about the brackets? (f) Should the retrospective bracket-normalized call-1 diagnostic (6/8) be reported, labelled retrospective and non-evidential, or left out?
